YOU ARE THE CONTROLS PROGRAMMER

Commission
the entire line.

Three PLCs. Three remote I/O racks. Three drives. One HMI. The machinery is installed. Nothing is addressed, mapped, downloaded, or programmed.

Open your project brief and functional specification

Deliverable: commission a 12 part batch. Eight good parts must reach dispatch and four marked parts must go to reject. The inspection sensor marks every third part as bad. Start is momentary, Stop must unlatch the system, and a cleared fault must never restart production without a new Start.

P1 • Infeed: A feeds stop gate B. Program the conveyors and gate release. B transfers to C only after P1 requests a transfer and P2 announces it is ready.

P2 • Lift and inspection: receive at C, raise to UPPER_C, then lower to LOWER_C before conveying to D. CYCLED_C remembers that the current part reached the top. D requests a transfer to P3 at E.

P3 • Sort and dispatch: receive at E. BAD_E marks reject parts. REJECT_E diverts them; accepted parts travel through F to dispatch. Dispatch can be blocked during testing.

Network contract: use unique host addresses on one /24 subnet. Enter the actual peer, I/O rack, and drive addresses in each PLC. Connections carry a snapshot of TX bits to RX bits on the next 100 ms scan. TX_RUN distributes run permission downstream. TX_REQUEST means a box is waiting at your sending station. TX_READY means your receiving station is empty and you can accept. TX_ACK must follow occupancy at that station within one second of transfer. Do not advertise READY or ACK incorrectly. TX_ALARM reports local faults and propagates downstream alarms back toward P1.

Fault handling: HEALTHY includes your peer connections, local I/O and drive readiness. SAFETY_OK reflects the independent simulated emergency stop circuit. DRIVE_READY includes drive setup and trip status. Propagate faults to the HMI, remove all O channel commands within one second of a stop, communication loss, drive trip, or emergency stop, then wait for a new Start after recovery.

HMI: connect to P1. Bind momentary Start, Stop and Reset tags plus running and alarm indicators. The HMI buttons communicate through those bindings. No controls are automatically wired for you.

Programming: choose an I channel for every sensor and an O channel for every actuator. Use those channel tags in each PLC program. M1 to M16 are internal memory bits. T1 to T8 are timers, C1 to C8 are counters. Download each draft, then switch that controller to RUN. Editing a draft does not modify the downloaded program.

This is a software commissioning simulator with simplified cyclic communication. It does not connect to real PLCs or implement a vendor protocol stack. Physical spacing and collision prevention are built into the transport model. Real safety engineering requires hardware and validation outside this game.

Factory acceptance test
The test runs isolated copies of your downloaded programs. It checks production, operator Stop, network loss, drive trip, emergency stop, and a blocked discharge. It also checks correct sorting, both transfer acknowledgments, HMI indication, and recovery without an automatic restart.
